finding: Native Runtime::open obtains the exclusive lease and verifies the configuration capture with a fresh MaterialVerifier. NativeRuntimeHost::new then constructs a separate empty verifier. Its first ensure/spawn verifies selected-plan materials again. The existing MaterialVerifier already reuses a matching hash within its instance after checking canonical path and device/inode/size/mtime/ctime signatures.
interpretation: This identifies a duplicate verification boundary and a possible admission-cost optimization. It is not a measured causal speedup and does not justify dropping identity checks.
candidate_design: Review carrying only the in-memory verified material cache from capture verification into the host under the same held runtime lease. Keep all capture/input/plan comparisons and every existing per-admission identity recheck. Do not introduce serialized proof, cross-process cache trust, copied-marker authority or shared competing ownership.
required_checks: Tampered bytes, same-size replacements, changed timestamps, changed expected hashes and symlink retargets still reject or rehash
Capture/configuration/plan mismatch still rejects independently of material cache
Fresh process and reacquired lease start from fresh identity verification
Measure separately shell readiness, capture admission, selected-model verification and actual model load on an uncontended window
